## Posterior Predictive Check


```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

plot_ppc <- function(models, observed = NULL, ndraws = 500, n_trials = 10000,
                     rt_range = c(0, 2.5), binwidth = 0.02, n_points = 512,
                     model_colors = c("#1E88E5", "#212121", "#FB8C00", "#6D4C41")) {

  if (is.null(names(models))) names(models) <- paste("Model", seq_along(models))

  # All models are checked against the same trials, passed in explicitly
  if (is.null(observed)) observed <- insight::get_data(models[[1]])

  # The predicted curve is the predictive RT distribution marginal over trials,
  # estimated by simulation. A random subset of trials estimates the same
  # distribution as all of them - each trial contributes ndraws simulated RTs
  # either way - so there is no reason to predict 320,000 trials x 50 draws
  # (16 million RTs per model, minutes per model) to draw a density curve that
  # 250,000 RTs already pin down. The histogram still uses every observed trial.
  pred_obs <- if (nrow(observed) > n_trials) {
    observed[sample.int(nrow(observed), n_trials), , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    observed
  }

  # Defective densities: each response's curve is scaled by its own rate, so the
  # two areas sum to 1 and correct/error are directly comparable across models
  defective_density <- function(rt, response) {
    keep <- is.finite(rt) & is.finite(response)
    rt <- rt[keep]
    response <- response[keep]
    purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1), function(r) {
      x <- rt[response == r]
      if (length(x) < 2) return(NULL)
      d <- density(x, from = rt_range[1], to = rt_range[2], n = n_points)
      data.frame(
        Response = factor(r, levels = c(0, 1)),
        x = d$x,
        y = d$y * (length(x) / length(rt)) * if (r == 0) 1 else -1
      )
    })
  }

  # Observed: histogram, put on the same defective-density scale
  obs_data <- observed |>
    mutate(bin = floor(RT / binwidth)) |>
    count(Error, bin, name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      x = (bin + 0.5) * binwidth,
      y = n / (nrow(observed) * binwidth) * if_else(Error == 0, 1, -1),
      Response = factor(Error, levels = c(0, 1))
    ) |>
    filter(x <= max(rt_range))

  # Predicted. brms::posterior_predict() calls the family's sampler once per
  # trial (thousands of calls of a few dozen draws each), and most of that is
  # fixed cost. cogmod's posterior_predict_<family>() methods take a vector of
  # observations, so the same draws come out of ~50 vectorised calls instead,
  # about 3x faster for the DDM - see ?posterior_predict_cogmod_ddm.
  predict_chunked <- function(m, newdata, ndraws, chunk = 50) {
    prep <- brms::prepare_predictions(m, newdata = newdata, ndraws = ndraws,
                                      allow_new_levels = TRUE)
    for (dp in names(prep$dpars)) prep$dpars[[dp]] <- brms::get_dpar(prep, dp)
    method <- get(paste0("posterior_predict_", m$family$name),
                  envir = asNamespace("cogmod"))
    chunks <- split(seq_len(prep$nobs), ceiling(seq_len(prep$nobs) / chunk))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, method, prep = prep))   # (draws * N) x 2
  }
  pred_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(m, nm) {
    pp <- predict_chunked(m, pred_obs, ndraws)
    rt   <- pp[, 1]
    resp <- pp[, 2]
    stopifnot(all(resp %in% c(0, 1)))
    defective_density(rt, resp) |> mutate(Model = nm)
  })
  pred_data$Model <- factor(pred_data$Model, levels = names(models))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col(
      data = obs_data,
      aes(fill = Response),
      width = binwidth, alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_data,
      aes(color = Model, group = interaction(Model, Response)),
      linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("0" = "#43A047", "1" = "#F44336"),
      labels = c("0" = "Correct", "1" = "Error")
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = setNames(model_colors[seq_along(models)], names(models))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rt_range) +
    labs(x = "RT", y = "Density", fill = "Observed", color = "Predicted") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.6))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

plot_ppc(
  list("LNR" = gam_lnr_muller, 
       "DDM" = gam_ddm4_muller),
  observed = insight::get_data(gam_lnr_muller),
  ndraws = 500
)
```
